title: Spanning Tree Root and Blocked-Port Investigation
summary: Investigate and resolve unexpected Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) root bridge elections and suboptimal blocked-port placement in a redundant multi-switch campus network. Diagnose root path costs, bridge IDs, and port states using Cisco IOS commands, deterministically configure primary and secondary root bridges, and ensure high-capacity distribution links remain unblocked while access uplinks safely absorb loop-prevention blocking.
learning_objectives: Analyze Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) bridge election criteria including bridge priority, system ID extension, and MAC address hierarchy
Investigate unintended root bridge takeovers using show spanning-tree and identify suboptimal transit path blockages
Calculate cumulative root path costs across mixed GigabitEthernet (cost 4) and FastEthernet (cost 19) links
Deterministically configure primary root (priority 4096) and secondary root (priority 8192) bridges using Cisco IOS commands
Verify that high-speed inter-switch distribution links transition to Forwarding while redundant edge uplinks correctly transition to Alternate/Blocking
Validate uninterrupted end-to-end host communication across redundant Layer 2 topologies

source.origin: Independently authored enterprise switching laboratory guide based on IEEE 802.1D / 802.1w standards and Cisco IOS Spanning Tree diagnostic best practices
